record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: Why do three-dimensional factorial moments, especially the second factorial cumulant K_2 = F_2 - 1, show similar scale-invariant behavior across lepton-hadron, hadron-hadron, and heavy-ion reactions; is this universality caused by a common Bose-Einstein origin of the fluctuations, and should such a large scale-invariant range occur in all cases?

evidence.quote: 4. The "Universality" problem. It has been noticed that 3−dimensional factorial moments follow a quite striking general behaviour in various reactions, such as lepton-hadron, hadron-hadron and even heavy-ion ones[11].

More precisely, the second factorial cumulant K2 (≡ F2 − 1) has roughly the same scale-invariant behaviour in all cases, up to a constant which can be attributed to the different long-range correlations. Is this feature due to the common Bose-Einstein origin of the expected fluctuations? Could we expect such a large extension of the scale-invariant range (from 1 to 104 subdivisions) in all cases?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider multiparticle production in high-energy collisions of three different reaction classes: lepton–hadron, hadron–hadron, and heavy-ion (nucleus–nucleus) reactions. For each event, partition a three-dimensional phase-space region (for example the cube spanned by rapidity, azimuthal angle, and transverse momentum, or by three components of momentum) into M equal cells, and let n_m be the number of produced charged particles in cell m. Define the normalized scaled factorial moments of order q by
   F_q(M) = ⟨ (1/M) Σ_{m=1}^M n_m(n_m−1)···(n_m−q+1) ⟩ / ⟨ (1/M) Σ_{m=1}^M n_m ⟩^q,
and the second factorial cumulant by K_2(M) = F_2(M) − 1.

Empirically, when log F_q(M) is plotted against log M in three-dimensional phase space, K_2(M) shows an approximately power-law (scale-invariant) increase, K_2(M) ∼ M^{φ_2}, with very similar exponent φ_2 across lepton–hadron, hadron–hadron, and heavy-ion reactions, differing essentially only by an additive constant attributable to long-range correlations, and persisting over a range from M = 1 up to about M = 10^4 subdivisions.

Provide a theoretical explanation of this approximate universality. In particular: (i) determine whether the common scale-invariant behaviour of K_2 in these three reaction classes can be derived from a common Bose–Einstein origin of the short-range two-particle correlations, and (ii) decide whether a scale-invariant range as wide as 1 ≤ M ≤ 10^4 should be expected on this basis in all three reaction classes.
artifact.category_tag: Factorial moments and intermittency in multiparticle production
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate active and ongoing investigation of the universality of three-dimensional factorial moments and their connection to Bose–Einstein correlations across lepton–hadron, hadron–hadron, and heavy-ion reactions. While partial explanations linking the short-range part of K_2 to Bose–Einstein correlations have been advanced and intermittency exponents are being measured in current heavy-ion programs (e.g., searches for the QCD critical point), no single decisive derivation establishes the observed cross-reaction universality and the extent of its scale-invariant range. The status is best described as unresolved/unknown in a definitive sense.

status_evidence.title: Universal intermittency in three dimensions and collective correlations in nuclear collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Multiplicity moments in three-dimensional phase-space bins exhibit simple universal features when analyzed in terms of cumulants.
status_evidence.claim: Universal features of 3D factorial cumulants across reactions are observed but their origin is discussed phenomenologically.

status_evidence.title: Intermittency and Bose-Einstein correlations
status_evidence.snippet: The role of Bose-Einstein correlations in the intermittency phenomenon has been reviewed.
status_evidence.claim: Bose–Einstein correlations are a leading candidate explanation for intermittency but a definitive universality proof is not given.

status_evidence.title: Search for critical point via intermittency analysis (CPOD 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Intermittency index φ2 expected to be 5/6 for a system freezing out at the QCD critical point assuming the 3-D Ising universality class.
status_evidence.claim: Current heavy-ion intermittency studies still actively measure φ2 to discriminate among universality classes, indicating the universality question remains under investigation.
